papers.title_in_file: Mode Selective Image Upconversion over Turbulence
papers.version_note: arXiv:1907.08715v1 preprint (19 Jul 2019, compiled 23 Jul 2019) in an Optica template whose header still reads 'Vol. X, No. X / April 2016'; the text layer is this paper.
papers.what_it_is: An experimental and numerical study of mode-selective sum-frequency upconversion of Laguerre-Gaussian modes in a PPLN crystal, where a feedback-optimized pump phase mask selects or deselects signal modes distorted by SLM-emulated turbulence.

assertions.value: The authors state that they account for turbulence indirectly, by modulating only the pump that drives the nonlinear process and not the images themselves.
quotes: here we account for the turbulence indirectly, by modulating only the pump driving the nonlinear process but not the images themselves.
assertions.certainty_reason: The abstract states the paper's own method; Sections 3 and 4 describe how it was run.

assertions.value: The authors report that their experimental results reached about 40 dB extinction without turbulence and about 20 dB in the presence of strong turbulence.
quotes: Our experimental results have achieved ∼40 dB extinction under no turbulence, and ∼20 dB even in the presence of strong turbulence.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study; the turbulence is emulated on a spatial light modulator.
assertions.reader_inference: The best measured values in Table 1(b) are 39.1 dB at SR = 1 and 20.7 dB at SR = 0.5; the Introduction rounds the strong-turbulence figure up to 21 dB.

assertions.value: The authors define the conversion extinction of two modes as the ratio of their converted SF power coupled into the fiber by the same pump.
quotes: The conversion extinction of two modes is then deﬁned as the ratio of their converted SF power coupled into the ﬁber by the same pump.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines its own figure of merit in Section 2; Table 1 repeats it in dB.

assertions.value: The authors state that any turbulence can be described by a unitary linear-optical transformation, so that distinct modes passing through turbulence have distorted profiles but remain orthogonal.
quotes: As any turbulence can be described by a unitary linearoptical transformation, distinct modes passing through turbulence will have distorted proﬁles but will nonetheless remain orthogonal.
assertions.certainty_reason: A premise stated without derivation or citation in this paper.
assertions.reader_inference: The experiment emulates turbulence as a phase mask on the signal SLM, which is a unitary operation by construction; the claim is not tested against real propagated turbulence with amplitude loss or scattering.

assertions.value: The authors state that they use sum frequency generation in a lithium niobate crystal where the signal and pump interact while experiencing strong diffraction, and that an optimized pump mode lets overlapping signals be upconverted selectively according to their orthogonal spatial modes.
quotes: where the signal and pump interact while experiencing strong diffraction.
By preparing the pump in an optimized mode, overlapping signals can be upconverted selectively according to their orthogonal spatial
assertions.certainty_reason: The Introduction states the regime and mechanism of the paper's own experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that a previous work of theirs studied selective upconversion of overlapping spatial modes in the non-diffraction regime with the same helicity for the signal and pump beams, and that this paper considers azimuthal indices from plus l to minus l for both beams.
quotes: In a previous work, we have studied the selective upconversion of overlapping spatial modes in the non-diffraction regime with the same helicity for the signal and pump beams [29].
Here, we consider azimuthal indices from +l to −l for both signal and pump beams.
assertions.certainty_reason: A description of earlier work by the same group, cited rather than shown here.

assertions.value: The authors state that the SF is described under the slowly-varying-envelope approximation by three coupled equations for the signal, pump and SF fields, and that they solve Eqs.(2)-(4) numerically with the standard split-step Fourier and adaptive step size methods.
quotes: The SF is described under the slowly-varying-envelope approximation as:
We use the standard split-step Fourier and adaptive step size methods
to numerically solve Eqs.(2)-(4) [54].
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of how its simulations are run.

assertions.value: The authors state that they use the Kolmogorov model to simulate refractive-index variation in atmospheric turbulence, with a refractive-index power spectral density equal to 0.0033 times the structure constant times the wave number to the power minus 11/3.
quotes: To study the turbulence effects, we use the Kolmogorov model to simulate the refractive index variation in the atmospheric turbulence [37].
assertions.certainty_reason: Eq.(5) is the paper's statement of its turbulence model.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer prints the exponent flat; the value says it in words. The experiment then adds turbulence phase noise to the SLM phase mask (see the setup assertion), not a propagation through a Kolmogorov medium.

assertions.value: The authors define turbulence strength approximately through the Strehl ratio SR, which varies between 0 and 1, with SR = 0 indicating the maximum turbulence and SR = 1 no turbulence.
quotes: SR varies between 0 and 1, with SR = 0 indicating the maximum turbulence
and SR=1 no turbulence.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines its own turbulence-strength scale below Eq.(6).
assertions.reader_inference: Eq.(6) is garbled in the text layer, so only the verbal range of SR is quoted.

assertions.value: The authors report that the pump and signal pulses are made by electro-optically modulating continuous lasers at 1544.9 nm and 1558.5 nm, with each pulse 200 ps at full width at half maximum and a 10 MHz repetition rate.
quotes: of continuous lasers, each at 1544.9 nm and 1558.5 nm.
Each pulse has a 200-ps full width at half maximum
(FWHM) and 10-MHz repetition rate.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors report a pump average power of 40 mW and peak power of 20 W, and a signal average power of 35 mW and peak power of 17.5 W.
quotes: The pump’s average power is 40 mW and peak power is 20 W.
The signal’s average power is 35 mW and peak power is 17.5
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its experimental setup.
assertions.reader_inference: The signal is a classical pulse of 17.5 W peak power, not a single-photon-level input; the Conclusion's mention of quantum light at the single-photon level is not tested here.

assertions.value: The authors report that the beams are magnified by telescopes to 2.6 mm FWHM for the signal and 2.8 mm for the pump, and are incident on Santec SLM-100 spatial light modulators at angles of incidence of 50 degrees and 55 degrees.
quotes: The beams are then magniﬁed by telescopes to 2.6 mm FWHM
for the signal and 2.8 mm for the pump.
incident on SLMs (Santec SLM-100) with the angle of incidences
of 50◦ and 55◦, respectively [29].
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its experimental setup.
assertions.reader_inference: The text gives the two angles after 'respectively' with the signal and pump beams as the subjects, so 50 degrees is read as the signal's and 55 degrees as the pump's.

assertions.value: The authors report a temperature-stabilized PPLN crystal with a poling period of 19.36 µm, doped with 5 mol.% MgO and 10 mm long, with 3 mm width.
quotes: stabilized PPLN crystal with a poling period of 19.36 µm (5
mol.% MgO doped PPLN, 10 mm length, 3 mm width, and 1
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that the signal and pump, both in Gaussian spatial modes, have beam waists inside the crystal of 45 µm and 41 µm respectively.
quotes: pump, both in Gaussian spatial modes, inside the crystal are
45 µm and 41 µm, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that the central wavelength of the SF light is 775.85 nm with a FWHM of 0.05 nm.
quotes: The central wavelength of the SF light is 775.85 nm
with FWHM of 0.05 nm.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that the SF light is coupled into a single mode fiber and detected by a power meter, and that this measurement is sent to a computer through a MATLAB interface to update the phase mask on the pump SLM and so optimize the selectivity among the signal modes.
quotes: The other arm of the SF light is coupled into a single mode ﬁber and detected by the power meter sensor
It updates the phase mask on pump SLM to optimize the selectivity among the signal modes.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its detection and feedback setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that the effect of turbulence on the signal is simulated by adding turbulence phase noises to the original phase mask for the LG modes.
quotes: The effect of the turbulence on the signal is simulated by adding turbulence phase noises to the original phase mask for the LG modes.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 3 states how turbulence enters the experiment, which limits what the turbulence results cover.
assertions.reader_inference: The turbulence is a static phase pattern written on the signal SLM; no free-space or time-varying turbulence path was used, so the results do not by themselves show operation over a real atmospheric channel.

assertions.value: The authors state that coupling the SF light into a single mode fiber before detection is necessary to achieve both high selectivity and high collection efficiency, which they describe as critical for photon-starving or cascaded quantum applications.
quotes: This is necessary to achieve
both high selectivity and high collection efﬁciency, as critical for
photon-starving and/or cascaded quantum applications [44, 55].
assertions.certainty_reason: An author statement of necessity, supported only by the comparison with the earlier image-plane measurement.

assertions.value: The authors report that, without turbulence, when the pump and signal azimuthal indices satisfy lp = minus ls the SF mode has a central Gaussian bright spot and thick outer rings, as expected, and that turbulence significantly reduces the total power and distorts the intensity profiles of the generated SF modes.
quotes: When lp = −ls, the SF mode has a central Gaussian bright spot and thick outer rings, as expected.
As seen, turbulence signiﬁcantly reduce the total power and distort the intensity proﬁles of the generated
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical and numerical observation from one study, read from figure images the text only describes.
assertions.reader_inference: No power figure is given for the loss under turbulence; the statement is qualitative.

assertions.value: The authors state that as SR decreases the strength of the turbulence increases and the spatial coherence degrades to give a distorted intensity distribution, and that at SR = 0.3 all modes become illegible.
quotes: From Eq.(6), as SR decreases, the strength of the turbulence increases, and the spatial coherence degrades to give distorted intensity distribution.
At SR = 0.3, all modes become illegible.
assertions.certainty_reason: An observation of the emulated turbulence from simulated and measured images in one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that their earlier experiment, measuring total SF power, achieved about 5.6 dB selectivity between signal modes LG00 and LG10 with an un-optimized pump in mode LG00, and that with the same pump the extinction rises to 15.9 dB when the fiber-coupled SF power is measured.
quotes: For instance, by measuring the total SF power, our previous experiment achieved ∼5.6 dB selectivity between two signal modes LG00 and LG10 with an un-optimized pump in mode LG00 [29].
With the same pump, the extinction is increased to 15.9 dB by measuring the ﬁber-coupled SF power.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical comparison from one study; the 5.6 dB figure is the group's earlier result.
assertions.reader_inference: The 5.6 dB baseline is cited from the group's earlier paper; only the 15.9 dB figure is measured in this work.

assertions.value: The authors report a fiber coupling efficiency of about 60% in the current setup for SF light created by a Gaussian signal and a Gaussian pump.
quotes: In the current setup, the ﬁber coupling efﬁciency is ∼60% for the SF light created by a Gaussian signal and a Gaussian pump.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, for the Gaussian-Gaussian case only.
assertions.reader_inference: The figure covers only the Gaussian signal and Gaussian pump case; no coupling efficiency or absolute conversion efficiency is given for the optimized pumps.

assertions.value: The authors state that a recent study they cite derived its extinction by selecting only the on-axis SF intensity of the central pixel on a CCD camera, and that its effective detection efficiency is therefore rather low.
quotes: In comparison, in a recent study [30], the extinction was derived by selecting the only on-axis SF intensity of the central pixel on a CCD camera.
Thus the effective detection efﬁciency is rather low.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' characterization of another group's method; no number is given.
assertions.reader_inference: The authors' own comparison, with no common benchmark between the two setups.

assertions.value: The authors state that a particle swarm optimization algorithm numerically optimizes the pump spatial profiles for the target signal modes, that the optimized phase masks are applied on the SLM, and that because of SLM phase errors and imperfect beam alignment the measured selectivity is significantly lower than achievable in simulation, so they add an adaptive feedback loop to fine tune the pump phase masks.
quotes: To further improve the selectivity, the particle swarm optimization algorithm is used to numerically optimize the pump
However, due to the inevitable phase errors in the SLM and imperfect alignment of the optical beam, the measured selectivity is signiﬁcantly lower than achievable in simulation.
To mitigate the errors and imperfections, we apply an adaptive feedback loop in our experiment to ﬁne tune the pump’s phase masks.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its optimization procedure.
assertions.reader_inference: The optimization needs a measured power signal from the fiber, so it requires enough SF power to read; the paper itself says weak SF power under strong turbulence degrades it.

assertions.value: The authors report that the pump S[LG00] is optimized to selectively upconvert signal mode LG00 while suppressing LG10, LG20, LG30, LG40 and LG50, both without turbulence (SR=1) and with the same turbulence noise (SR=0.5), and that xi_i is the dB ratio of fiber-coupled SF power of LG00 to LGi0 with the same pump.
quotes: Here, the pump S[LG00]SR is optimized to selectively upconvert signal mode LG00 while simultaneously suppressing LG10, LG20, LG30, LG40, and LG50 without turbulence (SR=1), and with the same turbulence noise (SR=0.5).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states which modes the Table 1 experiment covers: one target mode and five suppressed modes.
assertions.reader_inference: Only the five modes LG10 to LG50 were used as competitors; no result covers a larger mode set or modes other than the LGi0 family.

assertions.value: The authors report that in numerical simulations without turbulence the extinction reaches 44.4 dB, while the best experimental result gives 39.1 dB.
quotes: In numerical simulations, without turbulence the extinction reaches 44.4 dB, while the best experimental result gives 39.1 dB.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical and simulated result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: In Table 1 the values are 44.4 dB and 39.1 dB for xi_5 (LG00 over LG50). The smallest experimental extinction without turbulence is 27.2 dB (xi_1), so the ~40 dB headline is the best of five competitor modes, not the lowest.

assertions.value: The authors report that with the same pump S[LG00]SR=1 under turbulence the selectivity drops significantly, with the extinction reduced by about 23 dB on average in simulation and up to 18 dB in experiment.
quotes: As we add the turbulence, the selectivity obtained using the same pump S[LG00]SR=1 drops signiﬁcantly, with the extinction reduced by about 23 dB on average in simulation, and up to 18 dB in experiment.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical and simulated result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Table 1(b) as printed in the text layer lists xi_1 = 27.2 dB at SR = 1 and 4.7 dB at SR = 0.5 for the same pump, a drop of 22.5 dB, which is larger than the 'up to 18 dB' in the text. The simulated average drop from Table 1(a) is about 23 dB, which matches. The table values come from a garbled layer, so this mismatch should be checked against the PDF.

assertions.value: The authors report that re-optimizing the pump for turbulence with the same feedback method (S[LG00]SR=0.5) increases the extinctions by as high as 24 dB in simulation and 15 dB in experiment.
quotes: To overcome it, we then create re-optimized pump mode S[LG00]SR=0.5 using the same feedback method to recover the high extinctions.
As a result, the extinctions increase signiﬁcantly by as high as 24 dB in simulation and 15 dB in experiment.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical and simulated result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: From Table 1(b) the experimental gains are about 15.4, 9.3, 4.5, 5.2 and 0.1 dB across xi_1 to xi_5, so the 15 dB figure is the best case, for the first competitor mode only.

assertions.value: The authors state that in experiment the re-optimization significantly improves the measured extinction for the first LG modes but gives less improvement on the higher-order LG modes, because their current optimization method emphasizes increasing the lowest extinction for the LG00 mode over all the other LG modes.
quotes: Note that in experiment, while the re-optimization signiﬁcantly improves the measured extinction for the ﬁrst LG modes, it gives less improvement on the higher-order LG modes.
This is because our current optimization method emphasizes on increasing the lowest extinction to achieve high extinction of the LG00 mode over all of the other LG modes.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the limit and their explanation in Section 4.
assertions.reader_inference: The authors say the higher-order extinctions were already high and so improved only marginally; the table is consistent with this for the experimental xi_4 and xi_5 rows.

assertions.value: The authors report in the Introduction and Conclusion that the selective upconversion reaches up to 40 dB extinction without turbulence and up to 21 dB under strong turbulence, and that their experimental results match fairly well with numerical simulations without using any fitting parameter.
quotes: We demonstrate the selective upconversion of one LG modes against another with up to 40 dB extinction without turbulence, and up to 21 dB under strong turbulence.
Our experimental results match fairly well with numerical simulations without using any ﬁtting parameter.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, stated in the paper's summary.
assertions.reader_inference: Table 1 shows 44.4 dB simulated against 39.1 dB measured without turbulence and 31.8 dB simulated against 19.3 dB measured for xi_5 at SR = 0.5, so 'fairly well' covers gaps of 5 to 12 dB.

assertions.value: The authors report that the extinction drops as turbulence increases, and that for strong turbulence at SR=0.3 the average extinction for selecting LG00 still reaches an average of 16 dB in numerical results and 13 dB in experimental results.
quotes: As shown in Fig. 5 (b1)-(b4), when the turbulence increases, the extinction drops.
However, even for quite strong turbulence at SR=0.3, the average extinction still reaches an average of 16 dB and 13 dB for numeric and experimental results, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical and simulated result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The Abstract's 'maintains ~20 dB' is for SR = 0.5; at SR = 0.3 the experimental average is 13 dB by the text.

assertions.value: The authors report that for the mode they call LG01 the results are similar, with the average extinction dropping to 12 dB in simulation and 9 dB in experiment.
quotes: For the LG01 mode, we obtain similar results, as shown in Fig. 5 (c1)-(c4), with the average extinction drops to 12 dB and 9 dB in simulation and experiment.
(c1)-(c4) are similar results but to select LG10.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical and simulated result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The text says LG01 while the Fig. 5 caption says the target is LG10; the paper does not say which turbulence strength the 12 dB and 9 dB belong to, though they appear after the SR=0.3 sentence.

assertions.value: The authors state that with a straightforward modification of the convergence condition in the optimization algorithm the same technique can be used for mode deselection, where a certain mode is dropped rather than picked, and that a large negative extinction means a much lower conversion efficiency of the target mode versus others, which is desirable.
quotes: With straightforward modiﬁcation of the convergence condition in the optimization algorithm, the same technique can be employed for other operations, including mode deselection, where a certain mode is dropped, rather than picked, from other overlapping modes.
Here, a large negative extinction means a much lower conversion efﬁciency of the target mode versus others, which is desirable.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines deselection and its extinction sign convention in Section 4.

assertions.value: The authors report that the optimized pump D[LG10]SR=1 gives numerically evaluated extinctions of -33.6 dB, -31.2 dB, -24.8 dB, -29.0 dB and -24.2 dB, and experimentally observed extinctions of -26.3 dB, -24.4 dB, -20.2 dB, -17.7 dB and -11.9 dB, for the signal modes LG10, LG20, LG30, LG40 and LG50 respectively.
quotes: the optimized pump D[LG10]SR=1 gives the numerically evaluated extinctions -33.6 dB, -31.2 dB, -24.8 dB, -29.0 dB, and -24.2 dB
experimentally observed extinctions -26.3 dB, -24.4 dB, -20.2 dB, -17.7 dB, and -11.9 dB for the signal modes LG10, LG20, LG30, LG40, and LG50, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical and simulated result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper names the pump D[LG10] here, while the Fig. 6 caption and the surrounding text speak of deselecting LG00; the list's first entry is for LG10, so the naming is inconsistent in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors report that in experiment the re-optimized pump modes for turbulence give extinctions of -23.7 dB, -21.6 dB, -18.4 dB, -19.0 dB and -7.0 dB for SR = 0.8; -23.5 dB, -16.5 dB, -17.7 dB, -13.0 dB and -10.7 dB for SR = 0.5; and -12.7 dB, -16.2 dB, -15.7 dB, -11.1 dB and -3.9 dB for SR = 0.3.
quotes: In experiment, the use of re-optimized pump modes for turbulence give extinctions of (b2) -23.7 dB, -21.6 dB, -18.4dB, -19.0 dB, and -7.0 dB for SR = 0.8;
and (b4) -12.7 dB, -16.2 dB, -15.7 dB, -11.1 dB, and -3.9 dB SR = 0.3, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The text does not label the five values with mode names here; they are read in the same LG10 to LG50 order as the SR = 1 list. At SR = 0.3 the experimental deselection of the fifth mode is only -3.9 dB.

assertions.value: The authors report that the simulated deselection extinctions are -26.5 dB, -22.1 dB, -14.1 dB, -27.5 dB and -21.7 dB for SR = 0.8; -26.1 dB, -21.8 dB, -17.8 dB, -23.0 dB and -31.8 dB for SR = 0.5; and -9.5 dB, -12.5 dB, -14.0 dB, -23.3 dB and -18.5 dB for SR = 0.3.
quotes: In comparison, simulated results are (b2) -26.5 dB, -22.1 dB, -14.1 dB, -27.5 dB,
assertions.certainty_reason: A simulated result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The five SR = 0.5 simulated values equal the xi values in Table 1(a) for the S[LG00]SR=0.5 row (26.1, 21.8, 17.8, 23.0, 31.8) with the sign reversed, which may point to a reuse of that data in Fig. 6.

assertions.value: The authors state that in the case of strong turbulence the extinctions are less recovered by pump re-optimization, because the initial fiber-coupled SF power is significantly less, so that the feedback control algorithm works less well.
quotes: In the case of strong turbulence, the extinctions are less recovered by pump reoptimization.
This is because the initial ﬁber-coupled SF power is signiﬁcantly less, so that the feedback control algorithm works less well.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the limit and their explanation in Section 4.
assertions.reader_inference: The explanation is the authors' own and is not tested, for example by raising the pump power.

assertions.value: The authors state that all of their experimental results are in good agreement with the numerical simulations.
quotes: All of our experimental results are in good agreement with the numerical simulations.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's summary judgment of their own comparison.
assertions.reader_inference: Section 4 elsewhere says the measured selectivity is significantly lower than achievable in simulation and that Fig. 4 agrees only qualitatively, so 'good agreement' is a loose statement.

assertions.value: The authors state that existing phase compensation methods, including adaptive optics, feedback, feed-forward and machine learning, all rely on applying phase or amplitude modulations directly onto the signals, which they say could induce excessive noise while being subject to limited capabilities.
quotes: All of them rely on applying phase or amplitude modulations directly onto the signals, which could induce excessive noise and noise while subject to limited capabilities.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim about prior work, with no comparison in this paper.
assertions.reader_inference: No existing compensation method was run for comparison, so the advantage over direct signal modulation is argued, not measured.

assertions.value: The authors state that the indirect compensation approach avoids any modulation loss or noise added to the signals while allowing more flexible operations, and that it fundamentally eliminates the signal modulation noise or loss.
quotes: This indirect compensation approach avoids any modulation loss or noise added to the signals while allowing more ﬂexible operations.
Hence, it fundamentally eliminates the signal modulation noise or loss,
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; no loss or noise measurement of the signal path is reported.
assertions.reader_inference: The claim concerns modulation loss only. The paper also reports a fiber coupling efficiency of about 60% for the Gaussian case and gives no absolute upconversion efficiency, so the overall detection efficiency of the scheme is not measured.

assertions.value: The authors state that any signal mode that is not converted remains in its original wavelength and quantum state, so it can be recycled for cascaded operations, and that the same technique applies to superposition modes, which correspond to a new set of modes in different spatial profiles.
quotes: Favorably, any signal mode that are not converted will remain in its original wavelength and quantum state.
The same technique applies to superposition modes, as they correspond a new set of modes in different spatial proﬁles.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim about capabilities not demonstrated in the experiments reported.
assertions.reader_inference: No experiment in the paper uses superposition modes, recycles unconverted light or measures the state of the unconverted light.

assertions.value: The authors state that the approach allows exceptional flexibility and capabilities in manipulating and detecting overlapping signals, including quantum light at a single photon level.
quotes: while also allowing exceptional ﬂexibility and capabilities in manipulating and detecting overlapping signals, including quantum light at a single photon level.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; the experiments use pulses of 17.5 W and 20 W peak power.
assertions.reader_inference: All reported measurements used classical pulses with milliwatt average power; no single-photon-level input was run, so this is an extrapolation.

assertions.value: The authors state that the strong-turbulence extinction is expected to be significantly increased by using a better optimization algorithm and higher pump power to enhance the conversion, which will be a subject of future studies.
quotes: The latter is expected to be signiﬁcantly increased by using better optimization algorithm and higher pump power to enhance the conversion, which will be a subject of our future studies.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state in the Conclusion that the strong-turbulence result is limited by the current algorithm and pump power.
assertions.reader_inference: The expected improvement is a forecast; the paper does not test it.

assertions.value: The authors state that high-order optical angular momentum states could be measured by efficient quantum state tomography using a serial or optical-loop setup similar to that in an earlier reference, and that the capabilities may prove useful for remote sensing, phase encryption and decryption, compressive imaging and quantum free-space optical communication.
quotes: They can thus be recycled for cascaded operations to realize complex functionalities.
efﬁcient quantum state tomography can be implemented on signals in high-order optical angular momentum states [60].
quantum free-space optical communication [63], and so on.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's prospect, not tested in this paper.
assertions.reader_inference: These applications are not run or modeled in the paper.
